The deck

Contact sheet first, then all nine slides in order. If your client hides remote images, click show images, or use the pinned links further down.

How to post this

1. Download the PDF and post it as a LinkedIn document post.
2. Document title, Case File No. 002, The 8,000 Dollar Night Phone
3. Paste the POST block as the caption. Nothing else goes in the post.
4. Paste the FIRST COMMENT block as your first comment right after posting.

The PDF

carousel.pdf · 2.42 MB, vector text

POST (paste as the caption, whole block)

A 200 plus person family trades company in Ohio paid an outside service 8,000 dollars a month to answer the phone.

That is the owner's own figure, said on the podcast he co-hosts. They put a voice platform on nights and weekends, kept their people on the day shift, and stopped staffing the hours nobody wanted.

The deck covers the build, the before and after, what onboarding takes, and where this does not work here.

We do this kind of analysis for Alaska businesses, free. If you want your operation looked at this way, say the word.

If you run an after hours line, what does it cost you once you count the service, the on-call pay and the jobs that booked somewhere else?

#HomeServices #FieldServiceManagement #AlaskaBusiness

FIRST COMMENT (paste right after posting)

No independent account of this deployment was found. Every figure here traces to the owner, the podcast he co-hosts, or his vendor, and the deck says so on the slides.

GATES. machine_qa PASS. layout_check WARN, 0 fails. variety_check WARN, 0 fails, median layout IoU 0.48, value arc 0.756. coherence_check WARN, 0 fails, 5 warns. logo_check PASS. caption_check PASS, 734 chars, hook 114. style_lint clean. assemble PASS, vector, 2.42 MB, 9 pages. No hard fails. THRESHOLD NOTE. 8.16 clears the 8.0 rung for a 3-plus revision run. Against the 8.3 base threshold for a 0 to 2 revision run this would be below by 0.14, so the count matters and it is recorded honestly rather than rounded up. THE NUMBER PREDATES THE LAST FIX. The scorer caught that the cover's printed invoice had never actually shipped, an edit anchor silently no-opped, and the ledger had recorded a technique that did not exist. That is now fixed and the cover carries a real bill. The three changes since scoring only improve the two lowest criteria, so 8.16 is conservative and is not re-inflated. KNOWN WEAKNESS. Slide 8's particle field is largely covered by its text plates. Opening it would have meant deleting the honest limit, the rung 1 answer or the Monday action, so the copy stayed and the weaker art shipped. THE CASE'S CEILING. Zero independent corroboration, six routes attempted. Every fact traces to the owner, the podcast he co-hosts, or his vendor, and both episodes carry vendor sponsor credits. The deck discloses this on slide 6 and in the first comment.

Honesty gate

Verdict REVISE then applied. Weakest sentence under a hostile reply, "Anchorage does not get a smooth overflow curve, it gets a handful of nights a year when every marginal furnace in town quits inside six hours." (survives, yes, after the honesty gate de-quantified it from 'eleven nights a year', which was our analysis wearing the clothes of a fetched local fact in front of the one audience with personal counter-evidence).

Automation changes this run

  • fix · engine · render.py reports each text node up to 600 characters instead of 80, so the coherence gate can see a full authored sentence
  • improvement · gates · style_lint.py now refuses the banned glyphs (curly quotes, curly apostrophes, em dash, en dash) in every mode, and gains a --render-dir mode that lints every RENDERED on-slide text node out of render_report.json for those glyphs plus prose colons. Wired into Phase 5 and Phase 7 of the run contract.
  • improvement · gates · variety_check.py persists closest_pair and closest_pairs (top five by layout_iou + image_corr) into its JSON report. Report-only; no threshold, rule or verdict changed.

Aftercare

  • Drafts arrive daily and you own the cadence. Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11am Alaska time is the strongest window for this one.
  • Paste the first comment source block within 60 seconds of posting, before the first reader gets there.
  • Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes. Threaded author replies are the single biggest reach lever you have.
  • At 48 hours, note the saves and the offer line replies. Saves are the number that matters for a document post.
